thread.title: Fund managers haven’t been this bearish on global growth since 2008: BAML survey - MarketWatch

author: William Watts
title: Fund managers haven’t been this bearish on global growth since 2008: BAML survey - MarketWatch
text:
Fund managers in October turned the most pessimistic on global growth prospects since the depths of the financial crisis in the fall of 2008, but aren’t yet negative enough to offer a contrarian buy signal, according to Bank of America Merrill Lynch.
“Investors are bearish on global growth, but not bearish enough to signal anything but a short-term bounce in risk assets,” said Michael Hartnett, the firm’s chief investment strategist, in a note.
The firm’s monthly survey found that a record 85% of respondents think the global economy is late in the cycle 11 percentage points above the previous high in December 2007 (see chart below).
Bank of America Merrill Lynch And when asked about the outlook for global economy over the next year, a net 38% of respondents said they expect deceleration, the highest reading since November 2008. Growth expectations peaked in January 2018 (see chart below).
The chart above also illustrates the disconnect between global and U.S. growth expectations. As to why optimism over global growth can be so weak with the U.S. economy still booming, the survey found that concerns about the Fed are causing U.S. hopes to wane.
Meanwhile, BAML’s proprietary Bull & Bear Indicator came in at 3.3 in October, unchanged from a month earlier and still above the 2.0 contrarian buy signal threshold. “We sell Q4 rallies,” Hartnett wrote.
Stocks were on an earnings-fueled rebound Tuesday but have a long way to go to undo the damage suffered last week, with the S&P 500 SPX, +1.82% still down 4.3% so far in October, leaving it with a year-to-date gain of 4.4% and trading around 5.1% below the all-time high set in late September.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +1.83% is off 3.3% so far this month, leaving it with a year-to-date rise of 3.5% as it trades around 5% shy of its record close.
Traders last week blamed in part a selloff in government bonds that sent the yield on the 10-year Treasury note TMUBMUSD10Y, +0.12% to a seven-year high above 3.26% for spooking stock traders last week, leading to a selloff that saw the Dow and S&P 500 on Wednesday post their biggest one-day declines since February.
Read: Here’s why stock-market investors suddenly freaked out over rising bond yields
But fund managers still put the pain point where investors would be lured away from equities by a sufficiently attractive 10-year yield well above the market. The survey found investors don’t expect a rotation from equities to bonds until the 10-year yield hits 3.7%, according to the average weighted response, the highest since the question was first included in the survey in March and 20 basis points higher than in April. Haven-buying of Treasurys in the wake of last week’s equity market rout saw the 10-year yield retreat to around 3.15%. Yields and debt prices move in opposite directions.
On the allocation front, managers didn’t budge much when it comes to global equities, holding steady at a net 22% overweight, near July’s recent low of net 19%. The survey found allocation to U.S. equities reversed much of the climb seen over the previous two months, falling 17 percentage points to a net 4% overweight, while Japan became the most favored equity region. Allocation to bonds fell 5 percentage points to 50% underweight, but still well off the record low of a net 69% underweight seen in February.
Trade war topped the list of tail-risk fears for a third straight month, with 35% of respondents citing it as their top worry. Quantitative tightening continued to make inroads, however, with 31% citing concerns about the Fed’s unwinding of its balance sheet as their top fear. A China slowdown was at the top of the list for 16% of respondents.
The long “FAANG+BAT” position remained the “most crowded” trade in the eyes of survey respondents. The double acronym refers to U.S. tech giants Facebook Inc. FB, +2.69% , Apple Inc. AAPL, +1.69% , Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, +2.61% , Netflix Inc. NFLX, +2.40% and Google parent Alphabet Inc. GOOG, +2.10% GOOGL, +2.27% combined with Chinese tech juggernauts Baidu Inc. BIDU, +1.18% , Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. BABA, +3.30% and Tencent Holdings Ltd 0700, -0.50% .
The survey took place Oct. 5 to Oct. 11, with 174 participants with $518 billion in assets under management participating in the global portion of the survey, BAML said.
